intro.text: You are on the interrupt board. The sensor is ringing, but the line is wired straight to me. Nothing happens.

problem.text: A sensor does not shout directly at the CPU. The interrupt line rings the controller. The controller decides what I should do. I am the output side, not the spinal cord.

clue.text: Find the controller socket. Route the interrupt line to the controller, not to me. The controller is the integration point.

check.text: Which part is the integration point?

retry.text: No. I am the output side. The controller is the integration point.

right.text: Exactly. The controller maps to the spinal cord in this analogy. It integrates the sensor's interrupt and wakes me. I am the output side.

handoff.text: Start at the sensor console on the first ledge above the ground. Follow the switchback: press the sensor pad, carry the route plug to the controller catwalk, and leave the CPU socket below alone. When the actuator opens, drop through its roof or walk into the exit chamber through the ground doorway.
